story_title: Wheat Yield Analysis: Varieties, Sites, and Temporal Trends
story_subtitle: Exploring yield performance across different wheat varieties, sites, and years (1931-1932)

story_pieces.narration: In 1931, 'Trebi' emerged as the top-performing variety with an average yield of 46.93 units, significantly outperforming others like 'No. 462' (45.67 units) and 'Wisconsin No. 38' (49.87 units).
story_pieces.question: Which wheat variety had the highest average yield in 1931, and how did it compare to other varieties?
story_pieces.visualization: grouped bar chart (variety vs. average yield)

story_pieces.narration: University Farm consistently yielded the highest results across all varieties in 1931, with 'Trebi' (63.83 units) and 'Wisconsin No. 38' (58.8 units) showing exceptional performance, while Waseca and Crookston had the lowest average yields.
story_pieces.question: Which site had the highest average yield across all varieties in 1931, and which sites were underperforming?
story_pieces.visualization: stacked bar chart (site vs. average yield per variety)

story_pieces.narration: From 1931 to 1932, 'Trebi' showed the most significant yield decline (-15.5%) in 1932, while 'Wisconsin No. 38' maintained stable performance, reflecting resilience to environmental changes.
story_pieces.question: How did wheat yields change from 1931 to 1932 for each variety, and which variety showed the most volatility?
story_pieces.visualization: bar chart race (variety vs. yield over years)

story_pieces.narration: The combination of 'Trebi' at Waseca in 1931 (63.83 units) and 'Wisconsin No. 38' at Waseca in 1931 (58.8 units) highlighted the best-performing variety-site pairs, whereas 'No. 475' at Grand Rapids (19.7 units) was an outlier.
story_pieces.question: Which variety-site combinations yielded the highest and lowest results, and what patterns emerge from these extremes?

story_pieces.narration: In 1932, 'Manchuria' showed the most dramatic yield drop (-41.5%) compared to 1931, while 'Glabron' had the highest yield increase (+15.3%), indicating varying resilience to external factors.
story_pieces.question: Which variety experienced the most significant yield change between 1931 and 1932, and what might explain these differences?
story_pieces.visualization: bubble chart (variety vs. yield change percentage)
